research_question: What does APY mean, how is it calculated, and how should savers compare it?

research_brief.purpose: Explain APY with Regulation DD sources and worked calculations.

research_brief.scope_limitations: U.S. deposit accounts; illustrative calculations assume constant rates.

sources.title: Regulation DD 1030.2 Definitions
sources.verification_note: APY reflects interest rate and compounding over 365 days; interest rate does not reflect compounding (quoted).

sources.title: Regulation DD Appendix A: APY Calculation
sources.verification_note: 365-day assumed term for accounts without maturity; principal and interest assumed on deposit for the term (quoted).

sources.title: Regulation DD 1030.8 Advertising
sources.verification_note: Rate of return stated as APY; interest rate not more conspicuous than APY (quoted).

sources.title: What is a money market account?
sources.verification_note: Deposit accounts at banks and credit unions; FDIC or NCUA insured up to $250,000 per owner; differ from money market funds (page reviewed Aug 28, 2026).

sources.title: Interest rate vs APR
sources.verification_note: APR is interest rate plus additional fees charged with the loan (quoted).

statistics.claim: A 4.00% nominal rate compounded monthly gives about 4.074% APY; daily about 4.081%.
statistics.method: Fin Loom calculation with the standard formula
